_comment: The road itself. Each LEG has two or more ROUTES you can swap between — for weather, for closures, or just for what you feel like. Waypoints are real lat/lon, dense enough that the polyline through them approximates true road distance (the app applies a 1.04 wiggle factor). Mileage, day splits and every stop's position are recomputed from this, so edit freely. 'risk' marks winter trouble; 'elev' is feet.

vehicle.name: 2023 Honda Accord Hybrid EX-L
vehicle.chainRule: FWD does NOT qualify for California's R2 exemption, which is 4WD/AWD only. Under R2 this car needs chains ON. Carry low-clearance cable-style devices sized to the sidewall — check the owner's manual for Honda's chain clearance restriction before buying.
vehicle.note: Low ground clearance and touring all-seasons. This is a car that should not be on a mountain interstate during a storm regardless of what's in the trunk.

routes.name: The Route 66 road
routes.character: The great one. Everything worth seeing between here and Memphis is strung along it.
routes.why: The Grand Canyon, Meteor Crater, the Painted Desert and 1,500 miles of old Route 66. If the weather cooperates there is no argument for taking anything else.
routes.costs: Two genuine winter obstacles — Flagstaff at 6,900 feet and the Panhandle ice belt.

waypoints.name: Tehachapi Pass
waypoints.note: Chain control posts here. Your FWD Accord needs chains ON under R2 — the exemption is AWD only.

waypoints.name: Barstow
waypoints.note: I-40 begins. One road for the next 2,400 miles.

waypoints.name: Kingman
waypoints.note: Below the snow line. Sleep here if Flagstaff is getting hit and go over in the morning.

waypoints.name: Williams
waypoints.note: Turn north here for the Grand Canyon.

waypoints.name: Flagstaff
waypoints.note: The most likely place on this whole trip to find the interstate closed. Check the forecast 48 hours out.

waypoints.name: Continental Divide
waypoints.note: High point of the drive. Rain west of here ends up in the Pacific.

waypoints.name: Amarillo
waypoints.note: Here to Little Rock is ice-storm country in late December. Chains do nothing on ice — the only move is to not drive that day.

waypoints.name: Asheville
waypoints.note: I-40 climbs through the Smokies to get here and does ice up. The Blue Ridge Parkway closes outright.

waypoints.name: Raleigh
waypoints.note: PLACEHOLDER until we know her mom's city. Only the last ~300 miles change.

routes.name: The low road
routes.character: The bail-out. Nothing above 4,600 feet the whole way across.
routes.why: If Flagstaff is buried or the Panhandle is icing, this gets you to North Carolina without ever climbing. Adds Tucson, El Paso and Dallas.
routes.costs: You lose the Grand Canyon, Meteor Crater and the Painted Desert — and you'd be driving most of the return route twice.

waypoints.name: Tejon Pass
waypoints.note: The Grapevine. Unavoidable on this route and it does close.

routes.name: The Gulf Coast
routes.character: Down through Atlanta and Montgomery to the water, then west along the coast.
routes.why: New Orleans over New Year's, the Gulf, Mobile, and the Legacy Museum in Montgomery. This is the interesting one.
routes.costs: Slower, and New Orleans on New Year's Eve means booking a room well ahead.

routes.name: The inland run
routes.character: Straight across through Birmingham, Jackson and Dallas.
routes.why: Faster and simpler if you're worn out by then, or if the coast is weathered in. Picks up Birmingham's Civil Rights Institute and Dallas.
routes.costs: Skips New Orleans and the Gulf entirely — which is most of what makes this leg worth doing.

routes.name: The desert road
routes.character: The low road home. Nothing repeated, nothing above 4,600 feet, best desert on the continent.
routes.why: San Antonio's River Walk, White Sands, Carlsbad, Saguaro and Joshua Tree. The safest winter route of the whole trip and also one of the best.
routes.costs: Los Angeles traffic at the end, and the Grapevine as the last obstacle.

waypoints.name: Van Horn
waypoints.note: Turn-off point for Carlsbad Caverns and for Marfa. Decide before you get here.

waypoints.name: Las Cruces
waypoints.note: East on US-70 for White Sands, then back. Worth every minute.

waypoints.name: Blythe
waypoints.note: Back in California, still 500 miles from home.

waypoints.name: Tejon Pass
waypoints.note: The Grapevine. Last obstacle of the trip and it closes more often than people expect.

routes.name: Up through Vegas
routes.character: Same desert as far as Phoenix, then north to Hoover Dam and Las Vegas instead of west into LA.
routes.why: Almost identical mileage, no Los Angeles traffic, and it adds Hoover Dam and the Strip. If she's never seen Vegas, this is a cheap way to.
routes.costs: You give up Joshua Tree and Palm Springs, and you still finish over Tehachapi.
